description:
A DFIR analyst needs to reconstruct the HTTP browsing session from a packet capture. Using tshark (Wireshark's command-line tool), extract all HTTP packets (requests and responses) from /home/ga/Documents/captures/http.cap and produce a CSV file at /home/ga/Documents/captures/http_session_timeline.csv.

The CSV must have a header row with exactly these column names:
frame_number,time_relative,source_ip,destination_ip,http_method,http_request_uri,http_host,http_response_code,http_content_type,frame_length

Field details:
- frame_number: packet frame number
- time_relative: seconds since capture start (decimal)
- source_ip: source IPv4 address
- destination_ip: destination IPv4 address
- http_method: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) for requests; empty for responses
- http_request_uri: request URI path for requests; empty for responses
- http_host: Host header value for requests; empty for responses
- http_response_code: status code (200, 304, etc.) for responses; empty for requests
- http_content_type: Content-Type for responses; empty for requests
- frame_length: total frame length in bytes

One row per HTTP packet, ordered by frame number (ascending).
